correctness.rationale: The mean return from y is |y-x|/a by the one-sided first hitting law of a Brownian motion with constant drift toward x; only that conditional mean enters the regeneration. Subtracting the stopped exit-potential identity from the renewal equation gives p times the mean time difference as the expected alarm contribution |y-x|/a+f(x)-f(y). Since f(z)=z(L-z)/(2D), its strict interior chord bound is |f(y)-f(x)|<(L/(2D))*|y-x| for y!=x. The killed alarm law has positive density, so every positive rate is strictly worse at A<=2, including equality. In dimensionless units the success probability is S/sinh(k), S=sinh(k*u)+sinh(k*(1-u)); integrating the killed Green kernel on either side uses integral_0^u (u-y)*sinh(k*y) dy=(sinh(k*u)-k*u)/k^2 and its reflected version, giving the stated exploratory and return terms. The derivatives at u=0 of these normalized terms are tanh(k/2)/k and (1-k/sinh(k))/A respectively. Their difference from the baseline slope 1/2 tends to 1/A-1/2, so for A>2 one first takes a large finite k, and only then a positive sufficiently small u. The derivative at zero rate is the r=0 Green integral of the same alarm bracket (divide the renewal identity by r and use p->1); independently integrating its two polynomial pieces gives 117623/800000000 at the witness. The independent replay `python3 /workspace/branches/brownian_review_check.py` bounds the mean strictly between 0.00439269746548251 and 0.00439269746548252 by exact rational odd-power sinh series bounds, below 0.00495. The witness calculation is not a substitute for the analytic all-rate threshold proof.

value.rationale: The exact drift-speed threshold answers whether any rate is worth trying in an existing model, and separates an all-rate strict obstruction from the weak-reset cutoff of 4. The constructive near-boundary argument and a certified failure of the local diagnostic make the distinction useful. The result is existential in position and rate, not an optimizer formula for every position.
